quick_skim.title: GeoTrain: Energy-Aware Automatic Parallelism for Foundation Model Training on Heterogeneous Geo-Distributed Resources
quick_skim.abstract: Training foundation models at the frontier typically requires large-scale dedicated and centralized clusters with fast interconnects - infrastructure that is prohibitively expensive and generally accessible only to well-resourced organizations. Decentralized training over pooled, geographically distributed GPUs offers an alternative, but introduces substantial heterogeneity in compute, memory, power, and network performance. Existing distributed training systems are primarily designed for clusters with fast, low-latency interconnects and typically use all available GPUs when configuring parallel training. In geo-distributed environments, however, slower devices and weak network links can become bottlenecks, while optimizing solely for throughput overlooks significant energy cost.   We present GeoTrain, an automatic parallelism system that jointly optimizes training performance and energy consumption for heterogeneous geo-distributed GPU environments. GeoTrain simultaneously selects GPUs, partitions model layers, and determines pipeline configurations while accounting for heterogeneous compute, memory, power, and network constraints. To efficiently explore this large combinatorial search space, GeoTrain employs an optimized memetic algorithm with specialized genetic operators and local search. Experiments with decoder-only Transformer models on real-world and simulated heterogeneous topologies demonstrate that GeoTrain reduces iteration time and energy consumption by up to $61.4\%$ and $11.7\%$, respectively, over the existing state-of-the-art approaches. It also finds the exact optimum on verifiable instances and scales beyond exact methods as the number of GPUs increases, while exposing favorable energy-time trade-offs, including cases where its time-optimal distributed training plan is both faster and more energy-efficient than the baselines.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: GeoTrain proposes energy-aware automatic parallelism for foundation model training on pooled geo-distributed GPUs, mitigating heterogeneity and weak network links that bottleneck conventional cluster-oriented systems.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 前沿基础模型训练依赖高速互联的集中式集群，地理分布式GPU池虽成本更低，却存在算力、内存、功耗与网络的显著异构瓶颈。作者提出GeoTrain能耗感知自动并行方案，针对地理分布式环境联合配置并行维度与资源使用，而非盲目使用全部GPU。实验表明该策略可缓解慢设备与弱链路造成的瓶颈，提升训练效率与能耗表现。该工作为资源受限机构在异构分布式资源上训练基础模型提供了可行路径。

quick_skim.title: Low-Latency MoE Inference in Space Data Centers: A Wireless-Power-Transfer Perspective
quick_skim.abstract: Space data centers (SpaceDCs) are emerging as platforms for large language models (LLMs), supported by continuous solar-energy harvesting and high-speed interconnections. The mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture supports distributed LLM inference by deploying experts across satellites. However, skewed expert activation creates uneven computation power demands despite uniform solar-power supply at the dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit (SSO). Consequently, active experts remain power-constrained while harvested power at idle experts is underused. These reduce inference efficiency and increase latency. To address this supply-demand mismatch, we propose the SpaceWPT framework, which uses inter-satellite laser-based wireless power transfer (WPT) to redistribute harvested power. The key design challenge is to balance the computation demands of power-donating and power-receiving satellites under WPT losses: transferring more power accelerates computation at the receiver but leaves less power for the donor. After deriving design principles that simplify WPT control, we characterize the resulting latency tradeoff through a tractable surrogate of average inference latency. Minimizing the surrogate yields a novel two-sided water-filling strategy that determines whether each active expert donates, retains, or receives power according to the water level and its WPT link efficiency. Simulations with Mixtral-8x7B and Phi-3.5-MoE show up to 29.25% lower inference latency than without WPT, with larger gains under more compact formations and higher transfer efficiencies.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: SpaceWPT targets distributed MoE inference across satellites where skewed expert activation causes power supply-demand mismatch, using inter-satellite laser wireless power transfer to rebalance energy and cut inference latency.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对太空数据中心中分布式卫星MoE推理的场景，专家激活偏斜造成计算功耗需求不均，而太阳能供给却相对均匀，使活跃专家受功率约束、空闲专家能量浪费。作者提出SpaceWPT框架，利用星间激光无线功率传输在专家之间调配能量以缓解供需错配。通过平衡活跃与空闲专家的功率，该框架降低推理延迟并提升效率。这为面向太空数据中心的分布式MoE推理提供了功率协同的新思路。
